renderings.data: ### We Have Seen This Movie Before: Deep Learning vs. Classical ML

When Deep Learning surged in 2012–2018, many students rushed to abandon **Classical ML** — **Linear & Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forests, and XGBoost** — calling them "old-fashioned."

Then **Grinsztajn, Oyallon & Varoquaux (NeurIPS 2022)** benchmarked 45 real-world tabular datasets and proved a humbling truth: **Random Forests and Gradient Boosted Trees STILL outperform Deep Learning on tabular data** — faster, cheaper, and more accurate! And the researchers who actually *invented* Transformers and LoRA were the ones who mastered linear algebra, probability, and classical ML first.
[Grinsztajn, Oyallon & Varoquaux — NeurIPS 2022 (Tree Models vs. Deep Learning)]

external_link.title: Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on tabular data?
external_link.description: Benchmark across 45 tabular datasets proving that Random Forests and Gradient Boosted Trees (XGBoost/HistGBT) still outperform deep neural networks in accuracy and speed.

renderings.data: **THE LESSON FOR TODAY:** Just as abandoning Random Forests and regression during the Deep Learning wave was a mistake, abandoning **probability, tokenization, embeddings, and classical ML** during the LLM wave is the exact same trap.
## Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly: Shortcuts vs. Foundations
Acknowledge fine-tuning as valuable for execution, then pivot into the 4 technical pillars.
Execution has never been faster. Today, ten lines of Python download an open-weights Transformer and fine-tune it on your dataset, or wire an API into an agent.

**Let us be honest and practical:** taking an existing pretrained architecture and tuning it on local data **is** today’s biggest shortcut — and **that shortcut is genuinely valuable!** In engineering, shipping a strong baseline fast matters.

**The trap for students and researchers** is mistaking that shortcut for mastery. The temptation today is to jump straight to **autonomous agents, giant frontier Transformers, and multimodal wrappers** — **trying to fly before learning to crawl and walk**.

```text
Stage    | Mathematical Core                 | Why Skipping It Hurts You                                                     
---------+-----------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Crawl | Conditional Probability & Tokens  | You treat prompts as magic spells instead of conditioning distributions       
2. Walk  | Embeddings (R^d) & Attention      | You cannot diagnose broken representations across languages or modalities     
3. Run   | Two Memories: Weights vs. Context | You pay O(n^2) context rent forever and never teach the model your domain     
4. Fly   | New Tokenizers, Speech & Agents   | You build wings designed for Congolese languages, low-resource audio & reality
```
**THESIS:** Crawling and walking are the mathematical muscles that let you **run** and **fly**. Let us walk through the four foundational pillars live in code.
## Pillar 1: LLMs Are Conditional Probability Machines
People often say *"LLMs are just next-token predictors."* Technically true — yet it misses the word that gives you control. I prefer a more exact name: **conditional probability machines**.
When an LLM predicts its next token $x_t$, it is not asking *"what word usually comes next?"* It is asking *"what token comes next, **given** everything before the vertical bar `|`?"*
$$P_{\theta}(y_{1}, \dots, y_{T} \mid \mathrm{context}) = \prod_{t=1}^{T} P_{\theta}\!\left(y_{t} \;\middle|\; \mathrm{context},\, y_{1}, \dots, y_{t-1}\right)$$

**What "given" (`|`) means mathematically:** Conditioning means **narrowing the world, then recounting**. Out of all $N$ possible conversations, throw away every world where condition $B$ is false, and recount how often $A$ happens inside what remains:

stack.code: text(r"$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|B|} = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}, \qquad P_\theta(x_t = v \mid x_{<t}) = \frac{\exp(z_v / \tau)}{\sum_{u \in V} \exp(z_u / \tau)}$$")

renderings.data: $$P(A \mid B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|B|} = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}, \qquad P_{\theta}(x_{t} = v \mid x_{<t}) = \frac{\exp(z_{v} / \tau)}{\sum_{u \in V} \exp(z_{u} / \tau)}$$

Notice two laws in the inspected numbers:
1. `"Max"` is **12%** likely in general, **34%** given a *puppy*, and **1%** given a *cybersecurity startup*. The model never changed; **the condition did**.
2. **$P(A \mid B) \neq P(B \mid A)$:** $P(\text{Max} \mid \text{puppy}) = 0.34$, whereas $P(\text{puppy} \mid \text{Max}) = 0.71$!

**Autoregressive Snowballing — Why Multi-Step Agents Fail Quickly:** Every token the model generates crosses the bar `|` and becomes *given* for the next step. Step through this 6-step loop (`→` or `j` to step over) when single-step accuracy is $p = 0.85$:

Look inside $P_{\theta}(x_{t} \mid x_{1}, \dots, x_{t-1})$: what are the $x_{i}$? Before any matrix multiplication, a **tokenizer** maps raw text into integer IDs from a finite vocabulary $V$. Most modern LLMs use **Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)**.

**Live Trace Demo #2 — How BPE Learns Merges Step-by-Step:** BPE starts with individual characters and repeatedly merges the single **most frequent adjacent pair**. Step through 4 merges on a tiny Tshiluba root corpus (`"kulonga"`, `"kulongesha"`):

renderings.data: ### Can We Build Something Better Than Naive BPE for Bantu Languages?

Tshiluba, Lingala, Swahili, and Kikongo are **agglutinative Bantu languages**: words assemble cleanly as `prefix + root + extension + final vowel`:
- **Tshiluba (`-long-` = learn):** `ku-long-a` *(to learn)* · `ku-long-esh-a` *(to teach)* · `mu-long-esh-i` *(teacher)*
- **Lingala (`-yekol-` = learn):** `ko-yekol-a` *(to learn)* · `ko-yekol-is-a` *(to teach)* · `mo-yekol-i` *(student)*

English BPE slices `kulongesha` into `["ku", "lo", "ng", "es", "ha"]` — destroying the shared root `-long-` and charging a **5.44x attention tax**!

**OPEN STUDENT THESIS DIRECTIONS ON TOKENIZATION:**
1. **Adapting a pretrained model without retraining from zero:** Extend $V$ with high-utility Bantu morphemes + initialize new embedding rows via constituent subword averages or cross-lingual alignment (FOCUS / WECHSEL).
2. **Beyond BPE:** Morpheme-aware **Unigram LM** segmentation, or **Byte Latent Transformers (BLT)** that group bytes dynamically by entropy rather than English frequency tables.
## Pillar 3: What Is an Embedding — Across Text, Image, Audio & Video?

Token IDs like `t = 1482` are arbitrary labels: ID `1483` is no closer in meaning to `1482` than ID `9`. To do calculus and reasoning, we map every discrete unit into a continuous vector space $\mathbb{R}^d$. **That vector is an embedding.**

**The Simple Mathematical Idea:** An embedding function $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}^d$ assigns each input $d$ coordinates so that **semantic similarity becomes geometric angle** (cosine similarity):
### Why Embeddings Are the Universal Bridge Across Every Modality

```text
Modality | Raw Signal X         | Basic Unit ("Token")          | Projection into Shared R^d                        
---------+----------------------+-------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------
Text     | Characters / Unicode | Subword / Morpheme ID t       | Lookup row: e = E[t] in R^d                       
Image    | Pixel grid H x W x 3 | 2D Patch (e.g. 16x16 pixels)  | Linear patch projection: e = W_img * patch + pos  
Audio    | 1D Waveform p(t)     | Log-Mel frame / acoustic unit | Conv + Encoder projection: e = f_aud(frame) in R^d
Video    | Frames T x H x W x 3 | 3D Spatiotemporal tubelet     | Tubelet projection: e = W_vid * tubelet + pos_3d  
```

$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{contrastive}} = -\log \frac{\exp\!\left(\cos(\mathbf{e}_{i}^{(m_{1})}, \mathbf{e}_{i}^{(m_{2})}) / \tau\right)}{\sum_{j=1}^{N} \exp\!\left(\cos(\mathbf{e}_{i}^{(m_{1})}, \mathbf{e}_{j}^{(m_{2})}) / \tau\right)}, \qquad \mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}\right)V$$

**Live Trace Demo #3 — One Shared Geometry Across 4 Modalities:** Contrastive training pulls matching concepts together ($\cos\theta \to 1$) and pushes unrelated concepts apart ($\cos\theta \to 0$). Step through this cross-modal loop around **"Water / Mâyi / Mai"**:

**Look at what just happened in the Environment panel:**
- Aligned Tshiluba text `"mâyi"`, Lingala speech `"mai"`, a Congo River image patch, and a pouring-water video tubelet all align at **cosine similarity 0.89–0.96**!
- Meanwhile, unadapted BPE-shattered `"mâyi"` sits at **0.19** — geometric noise! With embeddings, **Text, Images, Audio, and Video all speak the exact same linear algebra.**
## Pillar 4: Your LLM Has Two Memories — Weights vs. Context & Speech

Now write the conditional probability distribution with its learned parameters $\theta$ explicit: **$p_\theta(\text{answer} \mid \text{context})$**. There are **only two places** where knowledge can live:

stack.code: text(r"$$p_\theta(\mathrm{answer} \mid \mathrm{context}), \qquad T_W(\mathrm{context},\, x) = T_{W + \Delta W}(x), \qquad W' = W + BA \;\; (r \ll \min(d, k))$$")

renderings.data: $$p_{\theta}(\mathrm{answer} \mid \mathrm{context}), \qquad T_{W}(\mathrm{context},\, x) = T_{W + \Delta W}(x), \qquad W' = W + BA \;\; (r \ll \min(d, k))$$

1. **Non-parametric memory (`context`, right of `|` — *the binder*):** RAG, GraphRAG, MCP, tools, agent memory. Strip away the buzzwords and **every single one pastes tokens into the context window**. You pay $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ rent on every call, long contexts suffer *Context Rot* (in our NLDB 2024 study, 500 targeted words beat full 5,900-word papers!), and reading is transient: $T_{W}(c, x) = T_{W + \Delta W}(x)$ discards $\Delta W$ the instant the call ends.
2. **Parametric memory ($\theta$, *the weights*):** Updated via gradient descent or **LoRA** ($W' = W + BA$, $r \ll \min(d,k)$). **Context holds what you can write on a page; weights hold skills, grammar, and phonology you can only learn from examples.**

renderings.data: ### Low-Resource Congolese Speech Recognition (ASR) & Speech Translation

Why do **open weights ($\theta$)** matter so deeply in the DRC? Because millions of Congolese communicate primarily **by voice** in Lingala, Tshiluba, Swahili, and Kikongo — and you cannot teach tonal speech acoustics by pasting a prompt into a closed API!

In **LiSTra** (first English-to-Lingala speech translation baseline), we showed how cascaded pipelines (`Audio → ASR → Text → MT`) compound errors when orthography is scarce, whereas direct acoustic encoders map speech frames straight into shared semantic embeddings:
[Kabongo & Marivate 2021/2022 — LiSTra Speech Translation]

renderings.data: **Wide-Open Speech Research for UNH Students:** Standard discrete speech tokenizers (HuBERT / w2v-BERT $k$-means units) trained on English discard **pitch and tone contours** that distinguish words and verb tenses in Bantu languages. Building **tone-preserving speech encoders** + human-verified benchmarks (**IrokoBench**, **INJONGO**) is frontier science you can lead right here.

renderings.data: ## Where I Am Up To: Africa AI 100, SALELA BONGO LLC & DarAkili
Coming home to **Lubumbashi** — where my own BSc in Mathematics and Computer Science began — to share these foundations with you at **Université Nouveaux Horizons** means everything to me.

This month, I was honoured to be recognised in the inaugural **Africa AI 100 (2026)** by the **Oxford Global Think Tank** — **Portrait 24/100: *"Computing in Tshiluba"*** in *The Languages* field, alongside heroes, mentors, and colleagues **Vukosi Marivate**, **Moustapha Cisse**, **Jade Abbott**, **Kathleen Siminyu**, **Bonaventure F. P. Dossou**, and **Deborah Dormah Kanubala**.

renderings.data: **THE QUESTION THAT DRIVES WHAT I BUILD TODAY:** The Africa AI 100 report describes our field as *"giving African voices a place in the machine."* The next question is ours: **once machines speak our languages, who gets to learn how to build them?**

Most Africans speak at least two languages — often because our mother tongue alone rarely opens the door to university or work. **Language should never be a gate to knowledge.**

That is why, through my company **SALELA BONGO LLC**, I have been building **DarAkili** (`darakili.com`) with my friend **N'Dah Jean Kouagou, PhD**. We teach STEM, programming — and next, **AI and Machine Learning** — directly in **Lingala, Tshiluba, and Swahili**.
[DarAkili · SALELA BONGO LLC — darakili.com]

external_link.description: Audio-first multilingual STEM and AI education platform teaching in Lingala, Tshiluba, and Swahili so language is never a gate to knowledge.

renderings.data: **Audio-First, Built by Humans:** Lessons on DarAkili are primarily audio + clear visuals so researchers and engineers in Lubumbashi, Kinshasa, Kananga, and the diaspora can contribute without heavy video production. **Only humans can do this work today** — even frontier LLMs still cannot teach accurately in most Congolese languages.

**FOUR COMMITMENTS AS YOU LEAVE THIS HALL AT UNH LUBUMBASHI:**
1. **Crawl & Walk with Mathematical Rigor:** Master $P(y \mid x)$, BPE, embeddings in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and classical ML alongside deep learning.
2. **Design Better Conditions & Train Both Memories:** Use context for fast-changing facts and open weights ($\theta$, LoRA) for Congolese language & speech capabilities.
3. **Own Foundational Research:** Better Bantu tokenizers beyond BPE, tone-aware speech translation, and clean open benchmarks.
4. **Build Together (*Masakhane*):** Contribute open digital resources at **IndabaX DRC** and lessons on **DarAkili** (`darakili.com` · **SALELA BONGO LLC**) — so youth across Congo **build** the machines of tomorrow. *Tuasakidila · Matondo · Aksanti · Thank you!*
